sources.locator: [VERIFY] watches, drums and the morning markets

fragments.text: Up before the fourth watch to fire the griddle; sold out before the morning drum.
Has walked the same lane since dawn, calling the price in a voice everyone knows.
Put the awning up twice this morning; the wind took it the first time.
Carried sacks of grain from a barge to a warehouse until the light went.

sources.locator: [VERIFY] the boat at the Rainbow Bridge

fragments.text: Lowered the mast to pass under the bridge, to shouting from the crowd above.
Came out after dark with a cousin to eat, look at the lanterns and be seen.
Flour is dear this week, and the barges from the south are late.
The rent is due, and the landlord's man has already been round once.
Plans to spend the evening at the entertainment quarter, listening to a storyteller.
Ate a bowl of noodles standing up, between customers.
The wind is up from the north, and there is dust in everything.

ranks.story: [DRAFT] Fog, and then a street. The fog does not lift so much as agree, stall by stall, to be a market.
ranks.title: Sleepwalker

ranks.story: [DRAFT] Before dawn, a voice calls the price of cakes. The mind, not quite asleep, answers it.
ranks.title: Daydreamer

ranks.story: [DRAFT] The canal is brown and slow and full of boats. The mind has the feeling, faint and specific, of having stood on this bank before.
ranks.title: Light Sleeper

ranks.story: [DRAFT] Lanterns come on down the length of the street. Someone calls a name the mind almost knows.
ranks.title: Lucid Dreamer

ranks.story: [DRAFT] The market thins toward morning. The mind feels itself surfacing, or something like it.
ranks.title: Waking Mind
